data.title: Union Pacific Stock (UNP) Dips on News the CFO Is Stepping Down
data.description:
The stock of Union Pacific (UNP) is down slightly on Oct. 16 after the company announced that Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Jennifer Hamann will retire from the railroad in early 2027. The company has not announced who will succeed Hamann in the CFO role. Hamann was ​appointed CFO of the railroad operator in January ⁠2020, making her ​the first woman to hold ​the position at the company.

However, Hamann has worked at Union Pacific in a variety of roles since ​1992 and has held ​leadership positions across the company over the years. In a statement, Union Pacific said it will ‌announce her successor at an unspecified later date. The retirement of the CFO comes after Union Pacific agreed in 2025 to buy rival ​Norfolk Southern (NSC) for $85 billion.

The Norfolk Southern Deal

The Norfolk Southern acquisition, which is not yet finalized, would create ​the first coast-to-coast ​freight ⁠rail operator in the United States. Specifically, the deal would create a rail network that spans 50,000 miles across 43 U.S. states.The merger is now under review with ⁠U.S. ​transport regulators.

The deal to buy Norfolk Southern would also put about 40% of all rail freight in the U.S. into one company, raising competition concerns in an industry that is viewed as vital to the economy. Union Pacific currently operates west of the Mississippi River, while Norfolk Southern is mostly in the eastern part of America.

How the Norfolk Southern Deal Is Structured

Management said that Union Pacific is offering cash and stock to buy Norfolk Southern for $72 billion. Norfolk Southern's debt takes the company's enterprise value to $85 billion. If approved by regulators, the combined company will be called Union Pacific and have over 50,000 employees, most of them unionized.

The proposed merger would cut the number of major railroads in the U.S. to five from six and comes three years after a Norfolk Southern train carrying hazardous materials derailed in Ohio, causing a major disaster in the town of East Palestine. Analysts have said that Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern are betting that the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump, which is pushing deregulation, will approve the merger.

data.title: Strategy Stock (MSTR) Falls on Potential Exclusion from Indexes Under MSCI's New Rules
data.description:
Strategy (MSTR) stock was down more than 6% on Friday (at the time of writing) as MSCI approved rules proposed in August that could remove the Bitcoin (BTC) treasury company from indexes. The final list of affected firms will be available on November 11, with the changes scheduled to be implemented at the close of November 30.

Why MSTR Faces the Risk of Removal from Indexes

Under the new rules, MSCI will apply an initial core screen to determine whether an issuer has substantial operating assets. Issuers that fail the initial screening will face an exclusion screen based on five non-industry-specific financial ratios, and a security will be ineligible for index inclusion if it is flagged on four or more of the ratios.

Aside from Strategy, Japan's Metaplanet is on MSCI's list of potential deletions. Index inclusion is crucial as passive funds and other investors tracking benchmarks are required to hold the shares in the index.

data.title: Oracle Stock Is a Waiting Game, Says Top Investor
data.description:
Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) has become one of the more divisive stocks in the AI trade. The longtime database company has turned itself into a major supplier of computing power for AI developers, but its shares sit 59% below their highs as investors question how much it is spending to build data centers.

The question now is whether the lower share price is a buying opportunity or a sign that the stock has lost its luster.

One investor who sees room for the shares to climb is John Ballard, who contributes to The Motley Fool. Ballard, who ranks among the top 2% of investors on TipRanks, believes Oracle's huge order book could more than double the stock by 2029, as long as a few things go right.

Promotion

200% short exposure to ORCL with ORCZ

Ballard's case is built on remaining performance obligations (RPO), which are signed contracts that have not yet been booked as revenue. RPO reached $664 billion in Oracle's fiscal first quarter (August quarter). That is $209 billion more than a year earlier and $26 billion more than the prior quarter. Management expects about half of it to turn into sales within three years. Because the money is already under contract, Ballard sees it as a fairly reliable guide to future revenue, especially while the industry still cannot build AI capacity fast enough.

Recent results support that view. Cloud infrastructure revenue rose 121% year over year to $7.4 billion. GPU utilization was 97.9%, and capacity that came up for renewal was re-signed or resold at a 20% premium. For fiscal 2027, Oracle is guiding for at least $90 billion in revenue and adjusted EPS of $8.10. Ballard also points to industry data. Synergy Research Group found that generative AI cloud services grew 165%, with Oracle among the fastest growers outside the big three. Goldman Sachs expects the five largest U.S. hyperscalers to spend about $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2027.

On valuation, the stock trades at about 20 times earnings. Wall Street's average estimate for fiscal 2029 EPS is $15.80. If Oracle hits that number and keeps the same multiple, the shares would land near $316, almost 140% above the current price.

The 5-star investor is open about why the multiple is low. Oracle plans $90 billion to $95 billion in capital spending this fiscal year. Customer prepayments and similar deals should bring the net cash outlay down to $70 billion or less. Even so, free cash flow was negative $5 billion last quarter. A large share of the backlog also comes from a handful of customers. Any delay in getting data centers running could slow how quickly the backlog becomes revenue and leave earnings short of forecasts.

Nevertheless, Ballard argues that accelerating infrastructure growth, nearly full GPU usage, and the ability to raise prices on renewals make a believable bull case, provided Oracle builds on schedule. (To watch Ballard's track record, click here)

Most of the analyst community takes a similar stance. Based on a mix of 27 Buys, 5 Holds and 1 Sell, the stock receives a Strong Buy consensus rating. Over the next year, shares are expected to appreciate by 89%, given the average target clocks in at $245.39. (See Oracle stock forecast)

data.title: Stellantis (STLA) Workers Hold Strike Vote in Canada This Weekend
data.description:
Unionized workers at automaker Stellantis (STLA) are holding a strike vote in Canada this weekend (Oct. 17 and 18). The vote is being held as Unifor, the union representing the automaker, says contract negotiations with Stellantis are stuck and at a standstill. The strike vote involves more than 9,000 Stellantis workers in Canada.

"A strike authorization gives the bargaining committee the authority to call a strike if necessary, it does not automatically mean a strike will take place," said Unifor in a news release. "Strike action remains a last resort, but the ability to strike is an important part of collective bargaining and can help create the conditions for an agreement."

data.title: SpaceX Stock: 'The Proof Points Are Closer,' Says Evercore as It Raises Price Target
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock has a new vote of confidence from Evercore ISI. Analyst Kutgun Maral believes the company is closer to delivering results than many expect. "The proof points are closer than many appreciate," he wrote, as he raised his price target by about 20% to $275 from $230. Maral maintained an Outperform rating.

Investors remain concerned about the cost of SpaceX's AI expansion. However, Maral believes higher earnings could support a higher valuation despite those funding concerns.

Evercore Raises Its Earnings Forecast for SpaceX

Maral raised his estimate for SpaceX's 2029 adjusted EBITDA to $266 billion from $210 billion. That is a 27% increase. Adjusted EBITDA measures earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on SPCX

At the same time, he lowered the valuation multiple for SpaceX to 15.3 times adjusted EBITDA from 16.6 times. This reflects concerns about the cost of funding its AI expansion. However, the higher earnings forecast more than offset the lower multiple.

Evercore expects SpaceX to reach $104 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, above its $100 billion goal. Maral also expects 2.3 gigawatts of computing capacity online by year-end. He sees a chance for that figure to reach 2.7 gigawatts.

For 2027, Maral forecasts 6.5 gigawatts of computing capacity, above the Street estimate of 6.1 gigawatts.

Starship and Starlink Plans Face Important Tests in 2027

SpaceX's Starship program is drawing attention as the company works toward reusable rockets. Starship reached orbit and deployed its first V3 satellites on Flight 14. Maral expects SpaceX could prove the rocket's reusability within the next few flights.

Reusable rockets could lower launch costs and allow SpaceX to deploy more satellites. Each Starship flight could carry about 26 terabits per second of V3 satellite capacity. More launches could help Starlink expand its broadband network.

SpaceX is also preparing to expand Starlink Mobile. Its V2 mobile satellites are expected to launch in 2027. The spectrum deal with EchoStar (ECHO) is expected to close in late 2027, ahead of a potential service launch in the first half of 2028.

The mobile service could give SpaceX another source of revenue. However, the rollout depends on satellite launches and the completion of the spectrum deal.

SpaceX Plans to Expand Its AI Business Beyond Earth

Elon Musk has targeted the fourth quarter of 2027 for the first Starmind AI satellites. Maral sees the launch as an early test of SpaceX's plans to run computing systems in orbit.

Orbital computing is still at an early stage. SpaceX needs to show it can launch these satellites and run them as planned. If successful, the project could open another path for AI growth.

Maral also expects SpaceX to win more outside customers as it expands its ground-based computing capacity. Progress at Grok and related AI projects could support demand for these services. Still, SpaceX must show that revenue from these projects can cover the cost of expansion.

What Is the Price Target for SPCX Stock?

On TipRanks, SPCX has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 28 Buys, five Holds, and two Sell ratings. The average SpaceX price target of $217.50 implies nearly 49.53% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: CoreWeave vs. IREN: One AI Stock to Avoid, One to Embrace, Says Investor
data.description:
CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) and IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) are both under pressure today, as the market grows jittery about the rising borrowing costs facing AI cloud providers. The pullback adds to recent losses, leaving both stocks down more than 50% over the past year.

The two companies are in the same business. Both rent GPU computing power to AI developers, and both are spending heavily on data centers to keep up with demand. The difference is who pays for the buildout. CoreWeave relies mostly on debt and equity markets, and those markets have turned on the stock in recent weeks. IREN has convinced customers to pay for a large part of its hardware upfront.

That gap is a focal point in recent analyses by an investor using the moniker Infinity Curve (IC), who has been taking a look at both stocks. The investor keeps coming back to one question: once the chips are bought and the lenders are paid, how much is actually left for shareholders?

Promotion

Double your CRWV exposure with Tradr's CWVX

With CoreWeave, IC's concern starts with the bond market. CRWV shares have been hammered over the past week, while the company's five-year credit default swaps moved past 1,000 basis points, and its unsecured notes due 2031 fell far enough to yield close to 15%. IC notes that none of this means the company has missed a payment or broken a covenant. But for a business that depends on outside money to grow, a sharp jump in funding costs is hard to wave away.

The balance sheet shows why. At the end of June, CoreWeave carried about $35.6 billion in debt principal and $16.3 billion in operating lease liabilities, compared with $5.5 billion in unrestricted cash. Its free cash flow deficit grew from roughly $4.7 billion in Q1 to $5.7 billion in Q2.

The two pressures also reinforce each other. A September agreement lets CoreWeave sell up to 35 million shares. At the October 7 price, that block was worth about $3.1 billion. After the selloff, it was worth roughly $2.4 billion. Expensive debt makes selling stock more attractive, but a lower stock price means more dilution for every dollar raised.

On the other hand, the investor doesn't see a demand problem. Nothing suggests customers are walking away, and the company guided Q3 revenue to $3.45 billion to $3.60 billion. What matters to IC is whether new capacity brings in more cash on its own, rather than needing more corporate debt or new shares to fund it.

At around 1.6x consensus 2027 sales, the stock looks cheap for a company expected to more than double revenue. The investor argues, though, that a sales multiple ignores debt, leases, and the cost of replacing GPUs. As such, IC takes a bearish view here now. "I sold my CRWV shares a few days ago, and for now, I am staying on the sidelines until I see clearer confirmation that financing conditions are stabilizing," IC summed up, rating the stock a Sell. (To watch Infinity Curve's track record, click here)

IREN looks different to the investor because of how its assets age. GPUs need replacing every few years, but power connections, cooling systems and buildings can serve several generations of chips. Recent IREN customers have prepaid 45% to 55% of GPU costs, and lenders have covered up to about 90% of GPU spending on some deployments. With contracts bringing in more than $20 million per megawatt each year, management estimates the GPUs can pay for themselves in about two years. In effect, the first customer helps pay for infrastructure that will outlast its contract.

That's where IC sees the real upside. The next deployment starts with a site that's already partly paid for, so most new spending goes to chips rather than rebuilding everything. Each successful contract leaves IREN in a stronger position for the next one, and over time that could push returns well above what today's financial statements show. Management also says older GPUs can keep earning after their five-year depreciation period by moving from AI training to simpler inference work, which would improve the economics further.

The investor's main caveat is about cash. Most of IREN's operating cash flow in the June quarter came from customer prepayments for services not yet delivered, and collecting cash early isn't the same as generating free cash. The figure to watch is cash per megawatt after debt payments, maintenance and reserves.

On valuation, IREN trades at 5.64x forward EV/sales, below peers MARA at 8.30x and RIOT at 9.97x, two bitcoin miners also moving into AI infrastructure. Its expected revenue growth of about 143% is the highest in that group. It also trades at 8.43x forward EBITDA, with EBITDA growth projected at around 178%. With $4 billion in contracted annual revenue and plenty of capacity still to develop, IC thinks the market hasn't caught up to the AI buildout. "I continue to be bullish on IREN as the upside story goes beyond the first GPU cycle," IC wrapped up. "If the cost of computing is recovered by the customers in their funded deployments while the renewable energy and data center structure is left behind, profits will continue to get better with each cycle."

As such, Infinity Curve rates IREN stock a Buy.

On the Street, both stocks receive Moderate Buy consensus ratings and are projected to generate big gains. CRWV's $143.59 average price target points to 12-month returns of 126%. Meanwhile, IREN is expected to gain an even more impressive 183%, given the average target lands at $79.30. (See CRWV stock forecast or IREN stock forecast)

data.title: Google (GOOGL) Secures Access to CNN News Content for AI Training
data.description:
Google parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) has secured access to the news content of broadcaster CNN, which it will use to train artificial intelligence (AI) models and agents. CNN said it is joining forces with Alphabet and will use the technology company's AI capabilities to enhance its viewer engagement.

At the same time, Google gains access to CNN's content for AI-generated purposes and online responses in its search engine. However, CNN has not outlined how it will incorporate AI to drive audiences towards its content, which is mostly comprised of videos and television news reports. For Alphabet, the deal is more clear as it will provide additional content on which the company can train AI models.
data.author: Joel Baglole
